title: Grape and Rosemary Focaccia
changes_from_base: Cornmeal and a little sugar in the dough, rosemary-infused oil, and grapes pressed into the top; baked cooler and longer.
summary: A lightly sweet cornmeal focaccia with juicy grapes pressed into the top and a drizzle of rosemary oil.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: seedless red or black grapes, halved if large

steps.title: Rosemary oil
steps.text: Warm the 4 tbsp oil with the chopped rosemary over the lowest heat for 3-4 min, until it smells fragrant, then let it cool.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Combine the flour, cornmeal, yeast and 25 g sugar, add the warm water, 1 tbsp of the rosemary oil and the salt and mix into a soft, sticky mass. The cornmeal gives a sunny colour and a faint crunch.

steps.title: Folds
steps.text: Leave 15 min, then fold the dough over itself every 30 min, four times, until smooth and airy.

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Brush the tin with 2 tbsp of the rosemary oil, add the dough and coax it to the edges. Cover and leave about 1 h, until puffy.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Dimple the dough, push the grapes into it so they sit half-buried, scatter the pine nuts if using, then the sugar and flaky salt, and spoon over the remaining rosemary oil.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 30-35 min, until deep golden and the grapes have slumped and bubbled; the centre reads about 96 °C. The longer, cooler bake lets the juicy fruit cook without the sugar burning. Cool 20 min before cutting.

tips: Press the grapes in firmly or they roll off as the dough rises.
Seedless grapes save a lot of picking at the table.
A common mistake is baking too hot; the sugar on top burns before the fruit softens.
storage: Eat within 1 day at room temperature, or keep in the fridge for up to 3 days and warm at 180 °C for 5 min. Not ideal for freezing because the grapes go soft. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
